newsitem.title: GERMANY: E.Europe sunseed exports and crushings seen higher.
newsitem.headline: E.Europe sunseed exports and crushings seen higher.

text.p: Eastern European sunflowerseed exports in 1996/97 (Aug/July) were forecast at 505,000 tonnes against 463,000 tonnes in 95/96 and crushings in the same period at 2.44 million (2.20 million), the Oil World newsletter said.
The figures cover Albania, Bulgaria, former Czechoslovakia, Hungary, Romania and former Yugoslavia.
Sunseed crops in the region in 1996 rose to a record 3.15 million tonnes from 2.89 million in 1995 and an average 2.45 million tonnes recorded in the five years to 1994.
Oil World said the increase was due to area expansions and favourable weather, mostly in Hungary and Romania.
Hungary's crop was 100,000 tonnes up this year at 882,000.
Oil World estimated Romania's crop at 1.15 million tonnes, up 204,000 tonnes, but stressed figures were not yet reliable.
But Bulgaria harvested 520,000 tonnes after 660,000 last year and the government banned exports.
Most of the exports would go to the European Union, where prices were attractive, Oil World said.
EU domestic rapeseed supplies were down and Spanish sunflowerseed crop estimates had to be reduced. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
